title: The Kiln and the Hand
logline: A potter's family works a week's batch from wet clay to a fired pot, reading hardness, wetness, warmth and air in their hands long before any of it has a name.

object.note: Object 7 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From grain in the hands to clay in the hands: a potter's family reading hardness, wetness, warmth and air long before any of it has a name.

thread_out.thread: The elements in the potter's hands move out to the wind of an eastern landing site, where a voice has to be told apart from the weather.

requirements: An active traditional pottery household still working by hand
A complete firing cycle achievable within the filming window
A potter willing to have decisions, losses and orders filmed, not just the craft

lesson.in_simple_terms: Wet clay, dry clay and a fired pot are described as the same four qualities in different amounts: hardness, holding together, heat and movement, always found together. When the conditions change, as they do in the kiln, the thing itself changes.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: තද බව, බැඳී පැවතීම, උණුසුම, සෙලවීම යන ගුණ හතර සෑම දෙයකම එකට ඇති බවත්, ඒවායේ ප්‍රමාණයත් හේතුත් වෙනස් වන විට මැටි ගුලියක් පෝච්චියක් බවට පත් වන්නාක් මෙන් දෙයම වෙනස් වන බවත් අභිධර්මය කියයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma names four great elements: earth as hardness, water as cohesion, fire as heat that ripens, and air as distension and motion. None can arise or last apart from the other three; they arise in one group, support one another and cease together, and their different proportions give things different form, colour, taste and function, so that more earth and less water is solid like stone or wood while more water flows like oil. Matter never arises alone: the four elements always come with colour, smell, taste and nutritive essence, and the Margaya describes soil, stone, fire, water and wind as the same basic group with different elements predominating. A thing looks unchanged only while the conditions producing it stay the same; when strong heat comes near, it changes that series into something else, as fire turns a thing to ash.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film follows one batch through a working week: clay soaked until it binds, judged for firmness by hand at the wheel, dried in shade and wind, then fired. Each stage shows one quality giving way to another without a word of explanation, and the tap of a fired pot, ringing true or cracked, lets the viewer hear what heat has done to the clay.

key_terms.en: material group; the smallest unit in which matter arises
the eight inseparables present in every group

lesson.caution: The four elements are not the elements of alchemy or a rival to chemistry, and the texts do not prescribe 'balancing your elements'; they are simply qualities found in every physical thing.
lesson.builds_on: The measurer's attention rested on grain passing through the hands; here the same kind of working hands read the qualities of clay directly, and the body's labour becomes a way into what all matter is made of.
